summary: SL-111 added ScanStore.NotListedAtOrBelow (ScanStore.cs:142-163). It is an allocation-free read that follows each folder's last-folder-child chain over the SL-109 NotListed marks. It stores nothing and changes no Append, SetChildren or AddFlags code. All five criteria are met. The suite is 1088/1088, up from 1023. Real-tree Stops showed 0 differences (56 runs in build, 209 in validate), and the 5M stopped store stayed at 637.1 MiB retained. Spike 121 had already settled the read, so the effort went into tests: 57 of the 65 new tests are a Kind-byte-write grammar corpus that replaced a dropped fitness rule. Nothing in src calls the read yet.

learned.lesson: NotListedAtOrBelow is exact only for preorder registration with one SetChildren per whole block, and Scanner.cs carries no comment saying so (m6 was waived to SC-397, so Scanner.cs is untouched). A slice that edits Scanner._pending (:168) or FolderDone's push loop (~:397) has to learn the dependency from three places: the read's doc comment (ScanStore.cs:142-163), docs/design/SL-111-not-listed-below.md:55-62, and NotListedBelowTests. Read those first. The repo tests cannot see a SetChildren per block inside a folder bigger than the sweeps' 2,000-entry 'big'. The throwaway real-tree harnesses could have, but they were not committed.
learned.evidence: Build record: Scanner.cs untouched, m4-m6 waived to SC-395..397. Validate record: 'The one gap is a future registration in blocks with a SetChildren after each. The tests cannot see that.' O-020 waived.

learned.lesson: Order guards need a ragged-depth tree. A uniform tree cannot tell a queue from a stack. NotListedBelowTests.RaggedTree and RaggedOrder (about 15 folders, a junction after a last subfolder, a 4-deep last-subfolder chain) are the only ragged fixture. NotListedTests' SweepTree, SweepOrder, Store, Baseline, RunBaseline, StopAt and Options are now internal and shared. The sweep must stop through StopAt. With default options m\Layers is listed, the call numbers shift silently, and the NotScanned-Layers case is never fed. A non-vacuity floor ('no stop saw the container layer store committed as not scanned') now makes that visible.
learned.evidence: Spike 121 exp 1: queue order gave 0 mismatches on a uniform 3-ary 5-level tree but 975 in 137,486 comparisons on the ragged one. Build mutation: sweep with default options went red with that message.

learned.lesson: A model disposition that says 'drop the rule, write the escapes in the doc' was executed as a closed-grammar C# lexer plus a 55-row JSON corpus. The cause was that the finding carried a class_of ('Kind-byte marker write spellings') and O-015 was discharged only 'as a class' with a corpus whose rows pass. 57 of the 65 added tests serve no numbered criterion. The lexer is the only parser in the diff and had a defect. When a disposition carries class_of, say in the because text whether prose suffices or a corpus is required. Otherwise the builder reads the obligation as requiring the corpus.
learned.evidence: O-015 closed with tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/KindByteWriteCorpus.json and KindByteWriteCorpusTests. Build record: 57 passed (55 rows, a census, a corpus-shape Fact). Suite 1088 against baseline 1023. m1's disposition text: 'Remove the SL-111 block from .taad/fitness.yaml... write the full list of escapes into the design doc'.

learned.lesson: KindByteWriteCorpusTests' grammar refuses any raw Kind spelling it does not know, reads included (e.g. `is (byte)EntryKind.X`, a read into a local; corpus Q13 and Q14). The next slice that edits Store/** and adds such a read goes red until Grammar.Check is edited, even though nothing is wrong. The stripper also misses a marker write that follows a `//` comment containing `/*` (SC-398). The census is trustworthy only because no Store file holds `/*`, `*/` or a string containing `//` today.
learned.evidence: Code review round 1 drift item (declared in the design doc at :107-108). Code review round 2 R2-R2-1: six live-write lines returned 0 refusals from a verbatim copy of Grammar.Check (lines 38-83); the control `|= 0x80` returned 1. Waived to SC-398.

learned.lesson: After a validate mutation of src (here Scanner stack to queue) is reverted with git checkout, rebuild before running anything else. Source is restored but the mutated Core DLL stays in bin\Debug, and a harness that loads that DLL reports queue-order results. Check by reflection that the restored type is back, as the final run did for `_pending`.
learned.evidence: Validate record: first real-folder run used the leftover mutated DLL and showed 13 of 31 stopped stores reading false at the root. After a clean rebuild the same tree gave 0 differences in 209 runs.

learned.lesson: For a store-read slice with a conclusive spike, the production diff is tiny and the test and doc diff dominates. This slice touched 8 files and added 65 tests, but the read is one method at ScanStore.cs:142-163. Size by the test matrix and by any review disposition that expands into new test tooling, not by the read. Spike exp 2 measured a reconstruction because exp 1's code was absent from its clone, and that was still conservative: the spike gave 27-29 ms, and the real read's answers alone took 16-20 ms with whole passes 38-58 ms in Debug.
learned.evidence: Spike 121 exp 2 headline ('rebuilt read: exp-1 code absent'). Build: answers 16.1-18.5 ms, passes 38.3-42.4. Code review: slowest pass 58.3 ms. Validate: slowest 51.0, answers 20.3.

learned.lesson: A build halted by a provider session limit is not quality rework, but it leaves a built, unreviewed tree and a missing design record. Build attempt 2 audited attempt 1 (clean build, tests green), kept it, and wrote the doc. Count it separately when judging whether a slice 'ran build twice'. The critique (2 runs) and code review (2 runs) laps were both deliberate: findings first, dispositions second, and a second break-it round.
learned.evidence: build-slice #1: halted on 'You've hit your session limit'. build-slice #2: 'Attempt 1's work was unreviewed but sound... I kept it. I added what was missing: the design record'.

learned.lesson: For SC-393 (App wiring): a 'stopped partway' row is `!NotListed(i) && NotListedAtOrBelow(i)`, which is the strict-descendant reading (U-204), so no second read is needed. A cut folder commits nothing, so an unlisted folder has no registered children and its strict descendants are empty. The read throws ArgumentOutOfRangeException on an empty store (Count 0), and U-207 found ShowOutcome already throws over a Cancelled empty store, so the App must guard Count 0 first. A RootUnreadable root that opened but listed nothing reads true (m3).
learned.evidence: Design contract error_cases (At throws when (uint)index >= Count); cases 'Stops in calls 1-2 leave Count 0'; U-207 'ArgumentOutOfRangeException... The store holds 0 entries'; m3 disposition.

learned.lesson: The first code-review round attacked the production read (two mutations, including the real Scanner pushed first-first) and found nothing. Only the second, break-it round compiled a copy of the one new parser and fed it adversarial lines. For any slice whose diff adds a text-matching grammar or matcher, plan that second round up front and have it feed the matcher inputs the compiler accepts but the matcher might mis-tokenise.
learned.evidence: Code review round 1: 'I found nothing that needs fixing.' Round 2: R2-R2-1 with six reproducing lines.

candidates.title: Decide fix-or-retire for KindByteWriteCorpusTests: plant a real Kind-bit marker and see what already goes red, before spending SC-398 on the lexer
candidates.why: tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/KindByteWriteCorpusTests.cs and KindByteWriteCorpus.json are 57 of the 65 tests this slice added (55 corpus rows, a census, a corpus-shape Fact; suite 1088 against baseline 1023). They serve no numbered criterion. The design's taste_disagreements #5 called the rule premature. Grammar.Check (lines 38-83 per code review) has the stripper defect SC-398, and it refuses harmless read spellings (corpus Q13 and Q14), so it taxes every later Store/** edit. The only mutation anyone planted was the no-op `page.Kind[i] += 0;`, a probe of the grammar. Nobody measured whether a real unmasked 0x80 in the Kind byte already fails the existing rollup and charge tests (raw Kind reads at ScanStore.cs:96, :336, :353 and ScanStore.Rollup.cs:22, :42, :61, :79). Plant one at ScanStore.cs:259, count the red tests, then either delete the grammar if the existing tests catch it, or do SC-398. Rank it with SC-398, not after it.

payload.estimate_error: Opened medium size and medium risk. Size was slightly low. The production change is one method, but the diff touched 8 files with 65 new tests and a design doc, and 57 of those tests came from a review disposition (m1 and O-015) that expanded into a closed-grammar corpus the design never planned. The build also needed two laps, though the first stopped on a provider session limit and not on quality. Risk was about right to one tier high for the read itself. Spike 121 had already shown 0 differences in 501,265 folder checks and 27-29 ms for 100k rows, and nothing in build, review or validate contradicted the design on the read, the memory bound or the timing. The risk that materialised was in new test tooling (the stripper), not in the store.

lessons_judged.why: The design wrote its replay feeders fresh instead of using RollupOracle.Feed, recorded the block-wise-registration gap, and filed SC-394. The critique's m6 then re-found the exact gap the lesson names (no note at Scanner._pending or FolderDone), and the build still waived it to SC-397.

The design and critique re-read ListRoot. AppendRoot at :261 runs before the root's listing, so the sweep skips only calls 1-2 (Count 0). Critique m3 produced the doc wording that a RootUnreadable root which opened but listed nothing reads true.
The read's whole premise is a single-threaded depth-first scanner. Because no parallel scanner exists, 'made parallel' was modelled by an interleave replay feeder instead of a real parallel run.

The 637.1 MiB retained and ~146 MiB headroom figures led the design to compute the answer instead of storing a Kind bit or column. The stopped-peak test re-measured 637.1 retained and 653.6 peak with 0 bytes allocated by the read.
The read was added to the GC-heap budget test (NotListedBudgetTests) before `retained` is measured, so that test gates the 'no per-entry storage' claim. No column was added.

The design extended the existing NotListedBudgetTests generator and cited SC-368 and #487 when filing the block-wise-writer invariant as SC-394, rather than building a new 5M generator. The effect was modest.
No App or tree code changed in this slice.
Every build, test, publish and mutation run went through eng/dotnet.ps1. The first run installed SDK 10.0.401 into the worktree's gitignored .dotnet/.

missed.what: KindByteWriteCorpusTests Grammar.Check strips comments with two regexes that do not tokenise C#. A `//` or `/*` inside a string literal, a `/*` inside a `//` comment (a cited glob such as tests/*.cs with a later src/**/x), and a `//` comment ended by U+2028 or U+0085 each blank live code, so a Kind-byte marker write in that text gets 0 refusals. Round 1 only mutated the read and the Scanner. It never fed the one new parser the diff added. Check it should have run: feed the grammar the six lines above and require a refusal.
missed.caught_by: code-review second round (same gate, same slice); waived to SC-398

missed.what: The design's criterion-1 non-vacuity floor ('listed folders reading true >= stops that left a root') cannot be met, because a store whose root is NotListed holds no listed folder. The critique should have asked whether the floor is satisfiable in the stops that leave only a root. The builder silently rewrote it as `listedTrue >= stores - rootsNotListed` (NotListedBelowTests.cs:218, :301).
missed.caught_by: build rewrote it; code review recorded it as undeclared drift

missed.what: The design says the criterion-3 test's first pass is cold, but its own asserted shape (root, A and S read true, Pad false) runs the read before the timed passes. The first pass is cold for data and warm for the read's JIT. The critique checked that each criterion had a case with a command, not that the cold claim survived the test's own setup.
missed.caught_by: code review, as undeclared drift (ScanStoreRollupTimingTests.cs:170-171); immaterial against 58.3 ms vs 250 ms

unknowns: Why is window case T-003 red at HEAD (design and build-check both cite it, via lesson #505), and does a backlog item already cover it? SC-393 touches FolderTreeNode, so Q-128 requires T-003 at its validate and a red T-003 would block it.

What does the read cost on a real large store? The largest real store in this slice was 100,011 entries, and the 5M figures (51.0 ms worst pass, Debug only) are synthetic. Spike 121 measured Release at 29 ms. Does a real C:\ tree (about 1M folders) with a 100k-child folder keep the whole open under the window's 0.5 s once SC-393 wires the App?

Does the engine require a corpus to discharge a class_of obligation? The build read O-015 as 'requires a corpus whose rows pass', although m1's disposition asked only for prose in the design doc. If prose would have discharged it, the 57-test lexer was avoidable.
what_went_wrong: Build attempt 1 halted on the provider's session limit with a built but unreviewed tree and no design record (docs/design/SL-111-not-listed-below.md). Attempt 2 had to audit and then trust it. It was sound, but the audit was a lap of its own.

m1's disposition said to drop the fitness rule and list the escapes in the design doc. The build instead wrote a closed-grammar C# lexer, a 55-row JSON corpus and a census, because O-015 was closed as a class. That is 57 of the 65 new tests, none serving a numbered criterion. The lexer was the only parser in the diff and it was wrong (R2-R2-1).

O-015 was closed as a whole family ('Kind-byte marker write spellings') and then a missing member of the family was found in the same slice. It was waived to SC-398 as 'does not weigh a lap'. The class was known to be incomplete at ship time.

The first code-review round returned 'found nothing that needs fixing'. Only the second round found the one real defect, in the test-side grammar. Round 1 mutated the production read and the Scanner and never attacked the new parser.

Lesson #485 named the gap that the order dependency is written only in a doc comment and a design doc. Critique m6 re-found it and the disposition accepted it, but the build waived it (SC-397). Scanner.cs:168 and FolderDone still carry no warning. The same gap was named three times and not built.

Three of six critique findings (m4, m5, m6) were waived at build. m5 is a single comparison that would turn a malformed-block hang into a throw. m4 was built in the read (per-entry page lookup) but its straddling-page Fact was not. All six critique findings were minor and were dispositioned by a model, so they count as untriaged.

Validate's Scanner mutation left a mutated Core DLL in bin\Debug after git checkout. The first real-folder run used it and showed 13 of 31 stopped stores wrong at the root. Validate noticed, disclosed it and re-ran clean (0 differences), but the run was wasted.

The design's own text was inconsistent in two places the critique passed: an unsatisfiable non-vacuity floor, and a 'cold first pass' that its own pre-timing asserts warm. The builder changed the floor without declaring it, and code review had to flag both as drift.

filed.title: Show the subtree-unread answer in the App: a mark on stopped-tree rows and stopped-list rows whose folder has something below it not read. This includes the window cases (T-003, T-012 neighbourhood) and Q-114's WindowMutants run for an App diff.

Before any pause/resume, read-ahead, block-wise flush or parallel-listing slice changes how folders are registered, it must either:
- keep depth-first preorder with one SetChildren after each whole block, and add a sweep folder larger than one flush block to NotListedBelowTests; or
- replace NotListedAtOrBelow with a stored pending-subfolder count, plus a 5M memory test.
This extends SC-368's block-wise-writer invariant (lesson #485, #487) to the subtree read.
No case puts a child block across the 65,536-entry page boundary where the answer depends on reading the right page.
The read's loop ends only because each chain step moves to a strictly higher index.

The read's only unproven precondition ('Future scanner slices keep the same registration order and the single SetChildren per folder') is written in ScanStore's doc comment, the class remarks and docs/design/SL-111.
R2-R2-1 (minor): Grammar.Check removes block comments with one regex, then line comments with another.
